days.heading: Depart Pittsburgh after work
days.note: Do not go into Lisbon city with luggage and a car. Overnight hop to Europe, then on to Lisbon.

days.heading: Arrive Lisbon → Cascais

facts.label: Car
facts.valueHtml: Pick up mainland rental at LIS

facts.label: Plan
facts.valueHtml: Cascais, beach/promenade, optional Boca do Inferno

days.note: The win today is a smooth landing, groceries, pool/beach, and an early dinner. LIS → Cascais is ~33 km / 25–35 min by car. Bonus: you land right in the middle of Cascais' Arraial de Santo António street-fair week (~Jun 6–13) — expect lively Marchas Populares energy and a livelier, more crowded promenade than a quiet arrival day; parking may be tighter near the center.

spots.cost: Beach access free. Sunbed ~$2 parasol ~$1.50, locker ~$0.50, shower ~$1. On-site parking metered (bring coins).

spots.saveHtml: Save Bring your own beach mats/umbrella to skip the $2 sunbed + $1.50 parasol — a family could save ~$15.

      <h2>The value fallback with real landscape variety</h2>
      <p>Pick Portugal if you want the cheapest strong plan: Cascais/Sintra, Algarve coves and boats, then Madeira levadas, lava pools, cliffs, and villages on a simple three-base route.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="decision-brief" style="padding:18px 20px;border:1px solid var(--line);border-left:6px solid var(--c2);border-radius:12px;background:var(--paper);box-shadow:0 10px 28px rgba(30,32,28,.06)">

        <div>
          <p class="eyebrow" style="margin:0 0 8px;color:var(--c1)">Choose this if</p>
          <ul style="margin:0;padding-left:18px;color:var(--muted);line-height:1.55;font-size:.94rem">
          <li>It scores 38/50 and remains the clean value play: about $7.5k-$11.7k, 12 nights, one main country, and a simple all-TAP air shape.</li>
          <li>Novelty 5 and Ease 4 are the strengths: Sintra, Benagil/Ponta da Piedade, Porto Moniz, Sao Lourenco, and Madeira viewpoints with only three bases.</li>
          <li>Food, weather, and picky-kid coverage are solid, with apartments and familiar plain-food fallbacks throughout.</li>
          </ul>
        </div>
        <div>
          <p class="eyebrow" style="margin:0 0 8px;color:#a23625">Reasons to pause</p>
          <ul style="margin:0;padding-left:18px;color:var(--muted);line-height:1.55;font-size:.94rem">
          <li>Swim 2 is the honest weakness: June Atlantic water is roughly 63-70 F, so this is pools/coves/scenery more than warm open-water swimming.</li>
          <li>The Faro to Funchal leg is the fragile joint because seasonal frequency is limited; it should anchor the dates before lodging is locked.</li>
          <li>If warm swimming is the deciding factor, Portugal + Crete, Hawaii, Albania, or Turkey make a stronger case.</li>
          </ul>

  <section id="stays" class="divider">
    <div class="section-label">
      <p class="eyebrow">Where We Are Staying</p>
      <h2>Three home bases</h2>
      <p>Each base is chosen for easy parking and luggage, AC and a washer, and a pool wherever possible.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="bases">
      <div class="base b1"><div class="band"></div>
        <img class="bimg" src="https://images.pexels.com/photos/38206392/pexels-photo-38206392.jpeg" alt="Cascais">
        <div class="bbody">
          <span class="nights">2 nights · Jun 11–12</span>
          <h4>Cascais</h4><p class="dates">Arrival base</p>
          <p>Beachy and practical, with easier parking and luggage than Lisbon or Sintra — close enough for Sintra and west-coast day trips. LIS → Cascais ~33 km / 25–35 min.</p>
          <p class="book"><b>Book:</b> apartment/aparthotel with reserved parking, AC, washer. Stay Cascais/Estoril/Birre/Guincho-edge — not deep Sintra or central Lisbon.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="base b2"><div class="band"></div>
        <img class="bimg" src="https://images.pexels.com/photos/6553674/pexels-photo-6553674.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&w=1600" alt="Carvoeiro">
        <div class="bbody">
          <span class="nights">5 nights · Jun 13–17</span>
          <h4>Carvoeiro</h4><p class="dates">Algarve base</p>
          <p>Best single Algarve base: close to Algar Seco, Praia da Marinha, the Benagil coast, Slide & Splash, Ferragudo, and Silves — still day-trippable to Lagos / Ponta da Piedade.</p>
          <p class="book"><b>Book:</b> villa/apartment with pool, AC, washer, private parking. Best zones: Carvoeiro outskirts, Vale de Centeanes, Lagoa edge, Sesmarias, or near Ferragudo if parking is guaranteed.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="base b3"><div class="band"></div>
        <img class="bimg" src="https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/a/ad/The_seafront_at_Ponta_do_Sol%2C_Madeira%2C_Portugal.jpg" alt="Ponta do Sol">
        <div class="bbody">
          <span class="nights">5 nights · Jun 18–22</span>
          <h4>Ponta do Sol, Madeira</h4><p class="dates">Island base</p>
          <p>Pretty small-town feel and sunset coast, with good road access to Calheta, Funchal / Câmara de Lobos, Seixal / Porto Moniz, and the major hikes. FNC → Ponta do Sol ~40 km / 34–35 min.</p>
          <p class="book"><b>Book:</b> villa/apartment with private parking, AC, washer, pool if possible. Ask specifically whether the driveway is steep, narrow, or reverses uphill. Take the better property over the prettier town name.</p>
        </div>
      </div>

Plan Health-Check

What to lock, watch, and expect

A critical review of the plan against your family & June constraints — researched July 2026. Kids assumed 13 & 8 in June 2027.

Act now

Book the Madeira flight first

Faro → Funchal is TAP-only, ~2 flights/week (Mon/Thu, seasonal Jun–Sep) — the fragile joint of the whole trip. Airline schedules load ~11 months out, so June-2027 seats open around now. Let the FAO→FNC flight anchor your dates before you lock lodging. If no good same-day option, the fallback is FAO→Lisbon→FNC — it eats most of a day, so keep the transfer day (Day 8) activity-free.

Heads-up

June water is cool — a “pools & coves” trip

Atlantic in June runs ~63–70°F (Cascais coolest, Madeira warmest — cool, marginal for kids). Make a pool non-negotiable at all three stays (heated if possible) — that's where the kids swim daily. The west-Sintra beaches (Adraga, Guincho) are cold, windy & rough → paddle/photos, not swimming. Real water wins: Slide & Splash, Porto Moniz's pools, south-facing Algarve coves, and the villa pools.

Heads-up

PR8 works for 13 & 8 — with care

Both kids clear the “over-5” bar, so PR8 stays the signature hike — but it's exposed with cliff drop-offs and gets very windy. Go early, check the morning wind forecast, and keep the 8-year-old close on the narrow railed sections. And pre-book PR8 and Balcões on SIMplifica — mandatory timed slots since 2025 ($5/adult, ≤12 free); you can't just show up.

Heads-up

Benagil: boat or kayak only — swimming into the cave was banned in 2024 (fines up to $2,700). Quinta da Regaleira: timed-entry tickets — buy online ahead in peak June. Praia da Ursa (an alt for Adraga/Cabo da Roca): steep scramble — fine for your 13-yr-old, keep the 8-yr-old hand-in-hand.

Why a straight later shift costs an extra PTO day

Juneteenth (observed Fri Jun 18, 2027 — confirmed: Jun 19 is a Saturday) only saves a PTO day when it lands on a weekday in the middle of the trip, replacing a day you'd otherwise have to take off. In the original Jun 11 plan it does exactly that (Day 7, mid-Algarve). Shift the whole trip 7 days later (the rejected option) and Juneteenth becomes the pre-trip send-off evening instead — a day that needed zero PTO anyway, holiday or not. The trick is lost: the same 12 nights now spans 9 full workdays with no holiday to offset.

The alt: leave Thursday, land on Juneteenth itself

Depart Thu Jun 17 after work instead of Fri Jun 18. You still work the full day Thursday (no PTO for an evening flight), and you land in Cascais on Friday Jun 18 — Juneteenth itself — a day that would otherwise cost a PTO day if it weren't a holiday. Result: 8 PTO days, 12 nights, 1.50 nights/PTO — identical efficiency to the original plan — while the whole itinerary shifts 6 days later, landing the Ponta do Sol stay right over ~Jun 27, the Madeira Atlantic Festival's Funchal fireworks finale (2026 pattern; 2027 dates not yet published). Juneteenth is a US holiday, not Portuguese, so nothing on the ground in Portugal is affected by which day you land.

Downside vs. the original plan: this alt still misses Cascais' Santo António week (fixed at Jun 6–13), and the back half of the trip drifts a few days further into pricier late-June territory.

✓ The pick: leave a week earlier instead

Depart Thu Jun 10 after work, arrive Cascais Fri Jun 11. Same mechanic, same math: 0 PTO for the Thursday evening flight, and 8 PTO days, 12 nights, 1.50 nights/PTO — identical efficiency to both other options, because the 12-night span still fully brackets the Jun 18 Juneteenth holiday (it just lands mid-trip, on the Faro→Madeira transfer day, rather than on arrival day). The difference from the "Alt" option above: this one lands you inside Cascais' own Arraial de Santo António week (~Jun 6–13) on arrival day instead of catching the Madeira fireworks, and it sits inside the first-two-weeks-of-June cheap-fare window fare-trackers flag, rather than drifting toward pricier late-June rates.

Temps and per-item prices don't meaningfully move on a single week's shift either direction — the "June weather" and cost figures throughout this page hold for any of these four windows.

Pros of the adopted week-earlier dates

  • Catches Cascais' Santo António street-fair week (Arraial de Santo António, ~Jun 6–13, with its own Marchas Populares at Cascais Bay) — arrival day (Fri Jun 11) lands right in the middle of it.
  • Stays inside the cheapest fare window — fare-trackers specifically flag the first two weeks of June as one of the cheapest weeks to fly all summer.
  • Avoids the late-June accommodation creep that both later options run into as pricing drifts toward the July peak.

Cons of the adopted week-earlier dates

  • Misses the Madeira Atlantic Festival's closing fireworks entirely — Funchal ~Jun 27, per the 2026 pattern (2027 dates not yet published). You're home by Jun 23, days before it happens.
  • Sea water is at its coolest point of the four options — June water warms slightly as the month goes on, so this is the marginal low end (not dramatic either way).

Overall verdict

A straight 1-week-later shift isn't worth it — it costs an extra PTO day for nothing extra. Between the two 8-PTO / 1.50-ratio options, it's a straight trade: the adopted Jun 10 → Jun 23 dates catch Cascais' Santo António week and cheaper June fares; the Jun 17 → Jun 30 alt catches the Madeira fireworks instead but drifts into pricier late-June territory. Same PTO cost either way — pick the one whose bonus the family wants more. Santo António won out for this plan.

One more calendar quirk, unrelated to this decision but worth banking for future trips: July 4, 2027 falls on a Sunday, so most employers that observe it would give Monday, July 5 off instead — not usable for this trip, but a free day worth remembering.

Before you go — documents

Months ahead · don't leave to the airport

  • ETIAS is very likely required by June 2027. The EU authorization launches Q4 2026 with a ~6-month grace period, so plan on needing it. $20/adult; free for both kids but each still needs their own. Valid 3 years. Apply once the official portal opens — it isn't yet, so any site taking ETIAS applications today is a scam. Approval is usually instant but can take up to 30 days.
  • EES biometric borders are live. At your first EU entry (Lisbon) all four get a face photo; adults + the 13-yr-old also give fingerprints (under-12s exempt). No more passport stamps — but expect longer immigration lines on arrival, so build in buffer.
  • No Global Entry equivalent exists for Portugal/EU entry. The EU’s planned “Registered Traveller Programme” was scrapped in 2016 — ETIAS/EES are pre-authorization + biometric registration, not an expedited lane. Lisbon has e-gates (RAPID4ALL) confirmed for US passport holders; Faro/Funchal coverage for US citizens is unconfirmed — don’t count on it. ANA Fast Track speeds up security only, never immigration. The one prep option: pre-register biometrics up to 72h ahead via the free EU “Travel to Europe” app.
  • Check passports now. Must be valid ≥3 months beyond your June-2027 departure, issued within 10 years, with 2 blank pages. Kids' passports are only valid 5 years — the most common trip-killer.
  • Get an International Driving Permit from AAA (~$20) before you fly — Portugal officially requires it alongside your US license, and you can't get one there. Two passport photos, valid one year.

Flights & airports

Booking + day-of

  • Pay to seat all four together at booking. TAP doesn't guarantee families sit together and the app can split you — assign every seat when you buy.
  • ANA Fast Track security (~$11/person) is worth it at busy Lisbon in summer; skip it at quiet Funchal. Long layover? The ANA Lounge day pass at LIS is ~$30.
  • Give connections room: 2–3 hours at a European gateway with kids + checked bags on one ticket; 3–4 hours if you're self-connecting on separate tickets (you re-claim bags, clear immigration, re-check, re-screen).
  • Funchal is one of Europe's windiest airports — crosswinds routinely divert flights to Porto Santo. Don't book a tight same-day connection off your Funchal departure; keep the exit end flexible.

Arrival day — go private

Skip the rental counter on no sleep

  • Pre-book a private transfer for the arrival day and pick up the rental car on Day 2 in town. Jet-lagged with two kids + luggage, you skip the counter queue and driving on unfamiliar roads exhausted.
  • Lisbon airport → Cascais ≈ $65–110. Often cheaper and cleaner than a metered airport taxi (~$75–85 + luggage/toll add-ons).
  • Funchal airport → Ponta do Sol ≈ $50–65 (~37 min on the VR1 expressway).

Rental cars & driving

The counter + the road

  • Take the rental's own Via Verde toll transponder at the counter — not Easytoll (that's for foreign-plated cars). It auto-pays every electronic toll. The Algarve A22 is toll-free since 2025; you mainly pay the A2 south from Lisbon.
  • Your 8-year-old legally needs a booster seat (Portugal: under 12 and under 135 cm, ≈4′5″) — fines $130–650 per child. Bring one packable backless booster rather than renting twice across two cars and risking a no-show.
  • Decline the counter "Super CDW" (~$30–45/day). Book base CDW + a cheap standalone excess policy, and confirm it covers tires, glass and undercarriage — exactly the damage Portugal's potholes and Madeira's steep driveways cause. Bring a credit card for the $1,100–2,700 hold.
  • Don't drive into central Lisbon — camera-enforced low-emission zone (fines to $130) plus parking misery. Use the car only when leaving town.
  • Madeira: pay for an automatic with real power (≥~90 hp) — cheap manuals struggle on the grades. Load a parking app (Telpark / iParque) and keep coins for blue-zone meters, and fill the tank before the north/west — stations are sparse out there.

Hikes & timed tickets

Book ahead — several sell out

  • Madeira PR trails need a paid, timed SIMplifica reservation ($5/person; PR1 $12). Kids ≤12 are free but still need a booked slot. Save the emailed QR code — there's no signal in the mountains. Book as soon as your dates are firm.
  • PR1 (Pico do Arieiro → Pico Ruivo) reopened April 2026, now one-way; sunrise slots are the most contested on the island. Only hike it in a clear forecast, and weigh the pre-dawn wake-up + exposed midday heat for the 8-year-old.
  • Pena Palace (Sintra) sells out same-day — strict timed entry; book it before Regaleira. Buy Regaleira on the official site only (regaleira.pt).
  • Benagil boat/kayak and Madeira whale tours: book 2–4 weeks out for June — the small boats fill first.
  • Slide & Splash: buy online the night before (10% off, valid any date; the discount isn't sold day-of). Reserve small restaurants (e.g. Mama Mia, Carvoeiro) a few days ahead.

Smart timing & packing

Free, but decisive

  • Arrive before 9am at Praia da Marinha (only ~32 parking spots; police close the access road when it's full until ~3pm), Adraga, and Seixal.
  • Carry coins. Many parking meters and some beach facilities (toilets/showers) are coin-only.
  • Pack water shoes for the lava pools (Porto Moniz) and rocky coves, and a windbreaker — exposed clifftops and PR8 get genuinely cold and windy even in June.
  • Get an eSIM (Airalo/Holafly) before you land — you'll want data for maps, parking apps, and the SIMplifica trail QR codes on arrival. Strong sun on ridges and boats: hats + sunscreen.

What People Are Saying

Insider notes from people who've actually gone

Crowd-sourced from Reddit, TripAdvisor forums, and local-run blogs (July 2026) — the off-the-beaten-path stuff guidebooks skip. Reconfirm access rules, tides, and prices closer to travel.

Algarve caves & cove beaches

The famous ones changed the rules

  • Benagil is boat-only now. Swimming and self-kayaking into the cave are banned; take an early guided boat/SUP (before ~9am) for the best light inside and the calmest water.
  • Marinha & Vale Covo run on the tide. Come to Marinha before 9am at low tide (high tide pushes waves to the cliff base); Vale Covo, just east of Carvoeiro, only opens up at low tide down broken cliff stairs — near-empty, no facilities, water shoes.
  • Praia do Carvalho's secret door. Reached through a 15-m hand-carved tunnel in the cliff (spot the fossils in the rock) — long white sand, calm water, and deserted because the entrance is so obscure.

Carvoeiro on foot

Where the crowd isn't

  • Algar Seco: go left, go early. Everyone piles into the A Boneca cave; the trails to the left of the tunnel lead to quiet pools and rock formations. Before 10am or after 4pm; if the main lot's full, the uphill Rua das Flores lot usually isn't.
  • Seven Hanging Valleys isn't the "easy" family walk guides claim. Loose rock, unfenced cliff edges, and open sinkholes make it a real hazard for kids under ~10 or anyone with vertigo — 5.7 km each way.
  • Calm water for the little ones. The dramatic cliff beaches aren't the shallow-and-sheltered kind; Carvoeiro's own town beach, plus Burgau and Praia da Luz to the west, slope in gently with June lifeguards.

Where locals actually eat

Skip the waterfront markup

  • Cross the river to Ferragudo. Locals lunch at Toc Toc and Zé Morgadinho for the dish of the day; grilled sardines are best at lunch (caught overnight), not dinner.
  • Cascais percebes walk. Flat 20-min stroll from the marina to the Boca do Inferno cliffs (free); roadside marisqueiras toward Guincho serve percebes (goose barnacles) most tourists never try.
  • Mercado da Vila before 9am. Cascais' covered market (Wed & Sat) is best early for cheese, bread, and pastries — provisions for a picnic — before the 11am–1pm tourist rush.

Madeira: sun & poncha

Chase the microclimate

  • Ponta do Sol earns its name. Madeira's warmest, sunniest town — mountain-sheltered from the northern cloud — so it's often bright here (20–25°C in June) when Funchal is grey. Bank your beach/pool days for it.
  • Monte toboggan: cash and 9am. Take a taxi up to Monte and ride the wicker sled early — waits hit two hours after 10am, and the drivers often take cash only.
  • Drink real poncha. Skip the sweet passion-fruit tourist versions; ask for poncha regional (sugarcane rum, lemon, honey) at old-school spots like Taberna da Poncha or the hillside A Venda do André.
